project.name: KHKD - Kien Ba Khoang
project.description: Vietnamese science-horror Reel — kien ba khoang pederin bong da
project.story: The rove beetle (Paederus, called kien ba khoang in Vietnam) does not bite or sting, but its body fluid contains pederin, a toxin about 12 times more potent than cobra venom. When the beetle is crushed against skin, pederin spreads and causes painful linear blistering dermatitis. Vietnamese cities see outbreaks every rainy season as the beetles swarm toward fluorescent lights at night. The key advice: never slap or crush it on your skin — blow it away gently.
